seo.title: EmpowerHer Initiative
seo.description: A nonprofit organization empowering Afghan women and girls across the Middle East and Central Asia through mentorship, leadership development, educational support, storytelling, publication, and community engagement.

hero.heading: Empowering Dreams
hero.bodyText: At EmpowerHer, we believe every Afghan girl and woman has a story worth telling and a future worth fighting for. Through mentorship programs and publication opportunities, we help them find the tools, confidence, and platforms they need to raise their voices and become changemakers in their communities and beyond.

statsBar.heading: Abandoned Futures: Let Afghan Girls Learn
statsBar.bodyText: Since September 2021, all Afghan girls over the age of 12 have been banned from attending school.

stats.label: Girls have lost access to formal education.
School-aged Afghan girls (80%) are currently out of school.
Nearly 30% of Afghan girls have never attended primary school.

herVoiceContest.heading: HerVoice `2026`
herVoiceContest.bodyText: Courage, identity, and storytelling — by Afghan girls and women, written from within Afghanistan.

winners.name: Z.H.
winners.title: Bread and a Red Apple
winners.quote: I have turned the basement of my house into a school, a secret school for girls, to teach them everything that is forbidden.

winners.name: Roqia Qasemi
winners.title: When Did I Feel That I Am a Strong Girl?
winners.quote: You close the door, I will reach my dreams through the window. You beat me, I will use my blood as ink for my pen.

winners.name: Nazifa Popal
winners.title: What I Carried in My Voice
winners.quote: Every limitation had been, in its own crooked and unasked-for way, a preparation. And I had used all of it.

mission.heading: We see you. We hear you. `And we are with you.`
paragraphs: EmpowerHer was born from the hope and strength that you carry within you—even in the darkest of days. You are not forgotten. Your dreams, your voices, your potential—they matter. They are powerful, and they are needed in this world.

We know that many of you are facing unimaginable challenges. Barriers to education, threats to your freedom, and a world that too often refuses to see your worth. But we believe in your resilience. And through EmpowerHer, we are building a path forward—together.

Our mission is simple: to support you, to uplift you, and to walk beside you. Whether through education, mentorship, leadership workshops, or simply being a voice when yours is silenced, we are here for you.
Please don't give up. There is a growing community—inside and outside Afghanistan—that believes in your power to lead, to learn, and to rise. And we are proud to stand with you.

quotes.text: For too long, Afghan girls have been written into history as victims. This time, let's write our own.
quotes.name: Nahid Karimi

quotes.text: WE RISE, WE RISE, WE RISE IN THE FACE OF ADVERSITY
quotes.name: Mahdi Rahimi

programs.heading: Our Programs
programs.bodyText: Our projects are designed to meet Afghan girls where they are—and help them grow into who they're meant to be. Each initiative provides a safe, inclusive space where participants gain the tools, guidance, and community they need to rise. From leadership workshops to storytelling programs, every project builds confidence, sharpens skills, and encourages bold self-expression. Together, we're creating spaces where Afghan girls can learn, lead, and shape their own futures.

impactStory.heading: EmpowerHer in the News
impactStory.bodyText: Our mission to empower Afghan girls has been recognized and celebrated by local media, amplifying the voices of resilience and leadership within our community.
impactStory.subheadingBody: EmpowerHer was featured in a local Virginia newsletter through our former partnership with Rappahannock News. This acknowledgment underscored our mission to empower Afghan girls and amplify their narratives of resilience and leadership within a broader community.

features.label: Podcast
features.title: Interview with EmpowerHer Co-Founders
features.description: Our co-founders, Nahid Karimi and Mahdi Rahimi, joined the NSHSS Scholars Connect Podcast to share their personal journeys from Afghanistan to the United States and the experiences that inspired them to launch EmpowerHer. In this episode, they discuss the challenges facing Afghan girls under Taliban rule, the role of education and mentorship in creating opportunity, and how young people can transform adversity into meaningful impact and leadership.
